first_impression.reaction: Sophie here, with James reading over my shoulder. We came from a Google search for 'oceania wedding destinations' and we haven't picked anywhere yet. The intro is dry, but it's straight with us. 'What separates them for a wedding is the calendar and the paperwork' is the kind of line that makes me keep going, because nobody is promising us paradise. I skimmed the key takeaways, saw the cyclone season point straight away, and decided it was worth a proper read. It reads more like a briefing note than a magazine, which I'm fine with, but nothing on it makes me want the wedding.

journey.quote: What separates them for a wedding is the calendar and the paperwork.
journey.reaction: Good. That's honest, with no 'say I do in paradise' and no 'dream day'. I trust a page that opens on logistics.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller dates Fiji's cyclone season from November to April, so a covered ceremony space and a buffer day belong in the plan for much of the tropical South Pacific.
journey.reaction: This is useful. We're about 14 months out, so it's exactly the kind of thing that decides our month. I'd screenshot it for Mum.

journey.section: How we chose these Oceania destinations
journey.quote: The stations differ in period and in what counts as a rain day: Nadi covers 1961 to 1990, Apia 1971 to 2000 and Hamilton Island 2002 to 2026, so read each figure on its own terms.
journey.reaction: I appreciate the rigour, but this is where my eyes start to glaze. I'm a lawyer and I still don't need weather-station footnotes this early. I skimmed past it.

journey.quote: The trade-off is water on the ground: flooding is common in downtown Nadi and on the Coral Coast, and it can cut road access to the airport.
journey.reaction: This is exactly our grandparents worry. If the airport road floods, how does Nana get to the resort? I like that they say it out loud, and the venue question that follows is the one I'd have asked.

journey.quote: It also reports a National State of Disaster over worsening El Niño conditions, with possible water rationing.
journey.reaction: That gives me pause, and I'll be raising it with James. But I'd rather read it here than find out after paying deposits. It's an honest trade-off.

journey.quote: Can the covered ceremony space and the cyclone postponement terms be written into our contract?
journey.reaction: These venue questions are the best thing on the page. They sound like someone who has actually run these weddings. This is the 'insider' detail I look for.

journey.quote: Since 5 November, aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats have been barred from Santo International Airport until its rescue and firefighting services are fully running.
journey.reaction: Very specific and current. With 30 to 45 guests flying in from overseas, that alone takes Santo off our list. It's useful, if blunt.

journey.quote: Curfews and alcohol bans can come at short notice, flights may be suspended with little or no warning, and demonstrations may increase around 13 May, 24 September and elections.
journey.reaction: Fair enough, but this section reads like a government travel warning, and the whole entry is mostly warnings. It's honest, but I came here to get inspired and leave with a shortlist. I'd cross it off and move on.

journey.quote: Expect a request for a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) or Certificat de Célibat and a Certificat de Coutume, and possibly apostilles on Australian documents.
journey.reaction: This is the legal clarity I want, though it also tells me Tahiti means French paperwork I don't want to do myself. It makes me want someone to handle it, which is the point.

journey.quote: Check with the destination's authorities, or plan a symbolic ceremony.
journey.reaction: This line comes up again and again. For Fiji, the obvious headline option, I expected more than 'check with the authorities'. One of our goals is confidence that the legal side is sorted, and here the page puts it back on me.

journey.quote: With no flights on a Sunday, which day do guests leave, and do the inter-island ferries suit that day?
journey.reaction: That's the sort of thing I'd never have thought of, and it would ruin a guest weekend. Good catch.

journey.quote: On arrival you sign a declaration at a registry office, and the ceremony can only happen at the places on the application, so name a back-up venue.
journey.reaction: A clear, practical step with an insider tip. I like it.

journey.quote: Ask each venue how guests with limited mobility reach the ceremony across sand or by boat, where the nearest medical care is, and whether a Sunday rule touches your wedding weekend.
journey.reaction: Close, but it skips the part we actually lose sleep over: getting older guests from the airport to the venue. Half our list flies internationally, and this section assumes they all come from Australia.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Every planner says this. 'Single point of contact' is better than 'end-to-end', but I still don't know whether the Advisor knows the island or hands us off to a local stranger.

journey.section: Plan your Oceania wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Advisor quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: This speaks directly to my fear of hidden costs and currency surprises. It's the most reassuring line about the business on the page.

unanswered_questions: What does a wedding for 60 to 90 guests actually cost in Fiji or the Cook Islands, even as a broad range? The page gives no pricing at all.
Is there a real wedding we can look at, with the venue and date, at any of these places?
Does the Wedded Advisor know these islands personally, or are local vendors and coordinators people they've never worked with?
Who is accountable on the day if something goes wrong: our Advisor, or someone on the ground?
Can Fiji weddings be legal for Australians, and what are the steps? The page only says to check with the authorities.
Which of these places work best for a guest list where half fly in from outside Australia?
Is the AUD quote fixed, or does it move with exchange rates before final payment?

turn_offs_found.quote: Ten places, unranked, run from Fiji to Tahiti in four groups: Melanesia, Polynesia, New Zealand and the Whitsundays.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a cliché, but there are no ranges of any kind on this page, not even a rough budget band per destination. My persona lists vague pricing with no ranges as a turn-off. This page doesn't hide prices so much as leave them out completely.

would_share_with: James (my partner), mainly the at-a-glance table and the Fiji section
My parents, for the cyclone season and the buffer day advice, since they are contributing

cta_reaction.quote: Down to two islands and unsure which suits your guest list? Talk it through with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: It isn't pushy, which I like, and the fee-in-writing line helps. But we're not down to two islands yet, and we usually read two or three posts and one real wedding before we enquire. I'd bookmark this and come back. I wouldn't click today.

top_3_changes: In the guests section, name the airport-to-venue transfer explicitly, because that is the worry families actually have. Old: "Ask each venue how guests with limited mobility reach the ceremony across sand or by boat, where the nearest medical care is, and whether a Sunday rule touches your wedding weekend." New: "Ask each venue how guests get from the airport to the property, how guests with limited mobility reach the ceremony across sand or by boat, where the nearest medical care is, and whether a Sunday rule touches your wedding weekend."

Put guests alongside the calendar and paperwork in the intro, so that couples like us see the page is about our people as well as the rules. Old: "What separates them for a wedding is the calendar and the paperwork." New: "What separates them for a wedding is the calendar, the paperwork and how easily your guests get there."

Make the closing ask reflect a mixed guest list, so it feels like the brand understands couples whose guests aren't all in Sydney. Old: "which islands are on your list, your month and how many guests are travelling." New: "which islands are on your list, your month, how many guests are travelling and where they are flying from."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off carries an exact quote from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (early research, 60 to 90 guests, grandparents, hidden-cost fears)
No invented brand facts; gaps listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers, HTML comments and image slots treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, venue names, statistics, business details, legal claims or weather facts

assumptions: Persona is provisional (not CRM-calibrated), so reactions reflect the assumed profile.
Images were not visible (slots only), so the premium score rests on copy and tone alone; real photography could lift it.

open_questions.question: The persona strongly wants price ranges and a real wedding. Should a 'From AUD' range (with Nic's sign-off) or a link to a real Oceania wedding be considered in a later round? I have not suggested either because adding them is outside my edit limits.

For Fiji, the most likely shortlist entry, the legal line only says to check with the authorities. Is there a sourced legal route that could be added, or should the copy say plainly that a symbolic ceremony is the usual path?
